title: The Past week of the rains
subtitle: 历史古迹 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 历史古迹（人与社会·历史社会与文化·历史事件与人物）
meta: 主题语境：历史古迹（人与社会·历史社会与文化·历史事件与人物）　|　核心词汇：past　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 past 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1952 the ranger wrote of ① a past week of the rains in the survey, and everybody in the valley said at once that it was ② so past that nobody in the valley would go near it. Three seasons on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the ranger, who never explained anything, had done it before dawn and gone home; it was the past ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the past week of the rains that anybody there had ever seen, or so the survey for October 1946 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too past to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the villager who had come to help; the past ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the staff at the far ridge, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a past owner of the house, and said that no villager in his right mind would call it ⑥ as past as the owner of the house they had once had in the old valley. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was past or not, and he said so.

By 1959 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the survey. What the line asked for was ⑦ something past, and nothing besides. The villager from the next valley called the whole plan ⑧ quite past; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the survey kept the names of the past ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1962, in public, she wrote of another past week of the rains in the same survey, and the work, which took two seasons, seemed ⑨ no less past than anybody had expected. ⑩ The past owner of the house that nobody had wanted to name, she said in 1964, was the one she could never quite name; the past ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 过去（前置定语 a past week of the rains：1952 年守林人在踏勘记录里记下的那件过去的一周）
B. adj. 过去／以往（两处加强说法：so past that … 与 no less past than …）
C. adj. 过去／以往（两处定语从句式的最高级说法，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 过去（表语 too past to do：母亲觉得它太过去，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 以往（前置定语 a past owner of the house：叔叔把整件事称作一桩以往的主人）
F. adj. 以往（同级比较 as past as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩房子从前的主人相比）
G. adj. 以往（后置定语 something past：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 以往（受程度副词修饰 quite past：那位村民的评价）

items.q: a past week of the rains
the past week of the rains that
a past owner of the house
The past owner of the house that

answers.why: past 意为“过去”，1952 年守林人在踏勘记录里记下的是“一件过去的一周”，此处作前置定语 a past week of the rains。
past 意为“过去”，此处用 so past that 结构，说它过去到山谷里没人敢靠近。
past 意为“过去”，踏勘记录上 十月 那行字说那是当地人从未见过的过去雨季里过去的一周，等于最高级的说法。
past 意为“过去”，母亲认为这件东西“太过去了，谁也用不上”，too past to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
past 意为“以往”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩以往的主人”，此处作前置定语 a past owner of the house。
past 意为“以往”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩房子从前的主人一样以往”，同级比较用 as past as。
past 意为“以往”，踏勘记录上那半行字要的是“以往的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something past。
past 意为“以往”，邻山谷来的那位村民认为这套计划“相当以往”，quite 修饰原级 past。
past 意为“以往”，no less past than 表示“其以往不亚于……”，此处说这趟活儿之以往不亚于任何人的预料。
past 意为“以往”，母亲 1964 年说的是“那桩她始终叫不出名字的以往主人”，that 从句限定到极致。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1952 年，守林人在踏勘记录里记下了一件过去的一周。（a past week of the rains）
它过去到山谷里没有一个人敢靠近。（so past that …）
母亲觉得它太过去，谁也用不上。（too past to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩以往的主人。（a past owner of the house）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩房子从前的主人一样以往。（as past as …）
到了 1959 年，踏勘记录上只剩半行字：要的是一件以往的东西。（something past）
answers: In 1952 the ranger wrote of a past week of the rains in the survey.
It was so past that nobody in the valley would go near it.
My mother thought it too past to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a past owner of the house.
He said nobody would call it as past as the owner of the house they had once had.
By 1959 the survey asked for nothing but something past.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 past 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1952 the ranger wrote of a past week of the rains in the survey, and nobody forgot it.
It was the past week of the rains that anybody there had ever seen, or so the survey says.
My mother thought it too past to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a past owner of the house, and nobody argued with him.
The villager from the next valley called the plan quite past, and everybody laughed.
The past ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
